summary: workflow archive, workflow status, sync and the cached-pricing reader all use data.db. The writers (workflow archive, sync) merge a leftover archive.db from earlier releases into data.db through SQLite on every run before opening it (attached read-only by an escaped file: URI): other tables with INSERT OR IGNORE, resources through Upsert so search indexes them; WAL-only rows are included and existing data.db rows win. archive.db is never moved or deleted, and repeat merges are no-ops, so later commits by an older process are picked up without trusting file timestamps. workflow status and cached pricing never write; status compares archive.db with data.db read-only, by data.db's primary key across every shared table (also when an older archive declared a different key) (resources, models, pricing...), and prints a note while archive.db holds rows data.db lacks.
reason: Earlier releases archived into archive.db while sync wrote data.db. A file move was skipped when learning setup had already created data.db, an ignored WAL rename failure could hide rows, removing the legacy files could drop a concurrent older process's commit, and a merge from the read-only status path could upgrade data.db.
validated_outcome: TestArchiveDBPathMergesLegacyArchive: data.db pre-exists, legacy rows uncheckpointed in WAL; the read-only resolver writes nothing; the write path merges both rows, keeps the existing row, makes the merged row searchable, leaves archive.db in place, and merges a later legacy commit on the next run. TestLegacyArchiveURIEscapesPathSyntax attaches an archive under a directory named with '?', '#' and '%' (fails with the unescaped URI). TestLegacyArchivePendingCoversTypedTables flags a legacy-only model_pricing row. TestLegacyArchivePendingCoversOlderResourcesKey flags a legacy resources table keyed on id alone.
